messages:
sam: Heads up — profiler shows a perf regression after the kernel-selector change that landed yesterday. Long requests are getting served fine but short sequences are seeing large queuing delays and eventual eviction from KV cache.

lin: :eyes: can you paste the top-line flame/profile?

sam: quick snip from the tail of the trace:
```
P50 latency: long=42ms short=88ms
KV cache hit-rate: before=72% after=51%
Evictions/sec: 420 -> 1330
Batch formation skew: short sequences frequently delayed >20ms waiting for batch fill
Kernel chosen: fast-attn-v2 (prefers larger seqs), fallback: generic-rt
```

anya: hmm that hit-rate drop + evictions explains starvation for short requests. Did the selector bias toward kernels optimized for long sequences?

sam: yes — the selector heuristic now picks fast-attn-v2 for avg_seq_len > 64 and for mixed lanes it prefers pairing with long ones. That improves throughput but seems to cause short lane starvation at the queueing layer.

ryan: i ran a clu-sim with synthetic mix (70% short <16 tokens, 30% long >256). saw queue aging in short lane, credit depletion in our token-budget allocator.

sam: proposal: temporarily tighten token_budget_target for short lane and add a short-path reserve to protect from coalescing with long batches. config idea:
```
batching:
  token_budget_target_short: 48
  token_budget_target_long: 256
  max_batch_delay_ms: 10
  short_path_reserve_tokens: 128
  lane_weights:
    short: 0.65
    long: 0.35
```

lin: also consider kernel-selection guard: if short lane queue length > 2, prefer short-optimized kernel (fast-attn-v1) even if avg_seq suggests v2. That avoids cross-lane mixing that triggers evictions.

anya: agree. we should also instrument KV cache churn: add a small counter for per-tenant evictions caused by batch coalescing so we can correlate with tenant QoS drops.

ryan: i'll run the canary with these three changes: token budget for short, short-path reserve, kernel guard. start with 5% traffic on staging -> 5% prod.

sam: for visibility, add a regression alert: if short P95 latency increases >20% vs baseline for 5m, auto-disable new selector (roll back).

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout 1705504800 -> 1705506600, owner=ryan. :robot_face:

deploy-bot: canary started at 1705504800 (5% traffic). collecting p50/p95, kv-hit, evictions.

lin: quick note: don't forget to bump the kernel-match TTL — we saw thrash when kernel choices flip rapidly. make it 30s min.

sam: good catch. also adding a metric: kernel-switch-rate by tenant.

anya: after canary completes we should run a synthetic hero trace that alternates bursts of shorts and longs to validate no reintroduce of oscillation.

ryan: running now. first 10m looks promising: short P95 down from 88ms -> 34ms, evictions down ~60%.

sam: :thumbsup: if numbers hold, promote to 25% and keep alerting ramp. thanks all for quick turnaround.

lin: small follow-up: we should write up the selector heuristics in the repo README (why we bias, when to override). i can draft.

anya: logging todo: annotate eviction events with batch composition (n_short, n_long, chosen_kernel). that will make postmortems much faster.

ryan: noted. I'll post results at end of ramp.

sam: tracking ticket: INF-6241 (starvation/kv-evict regression). linking test vectors and config diffs once canary finished.

deploy-bot: canary completed at 1705506600 — metrics stable.

sam: closing loop: promoted to 25% at 1705507200, continuing to monitor. last check-in for now.
